Definition
[strictly convex function]

Source: petersen:page-0259

A function on a Riemannian manifold is (strictly) convex if its restriction to every nonconstant geodesic is (strictly) convex as a function of the affine parameter. The Lean statements are relative to an open set $U$ (``convex on $U$''), quantifying over the nonconstant geodesics that stay in $U$; this is what Section 4 requires, and the global notion is the case $U=M$.

Constant geodesics must be excluded: $f\circ c$ is then constant and cannot be strictly convex. The Lean predicate IsNonconstantGeodesicOn records this guard. The criterion used in Section 2 is $(f_0\circ c)''=\operatorname {Hess}f_0(\dot c,\dot c)>0$.
